title: Signal cancellation
statement: A log records integer labels from 0 to 100. Repeatedly cancel adjacent equal labels until no adjacent equal pair remains. Return the number of labels left. Cancellation can bring another equal pair together. The empty log returns zero. There are at most 100 labels; do not change the input.

lesson.summary: Process labels from left to right with a stack. If the incoming label equals the top, pop the top and consume the incoming label. Otherwise push it. Return the final stack size.
recognition: Only the most recent surviving label can cancel the incoming label.
Earlier cancellations can expose another matching top.
Keep a stack representing the fully reduced processed prefix.
lesson.invariant: After processing a prefix, the stack is its reduced sequence and has no adjacent equal labels. The next label can affect only the top.
lesson.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; each label is pushed at most once and popped at most once.
pitfalls: Popping an empty stack is invalid.
Deleting only original adjacent pairs misses pairs exposed by cancellation.
Deleting every occurrence of a duplicated value cancels nonadjacent labels incorrectly.

states.explanation: Start with an empty stack. The processed prefix reduces to the empty sequence.
Incoming label 1 has no equal stack top. Push it onto the retained sequence.
Incoming label 2 has no equal stack top. Push it onto the retained sequence.
Incoming label 2 equals the stack top. Pop that top and consume the incoming label as a cancelling pair.
Incoming label 1 equals the stack top. Pop that top and consume the incoming label as a cancelling pair.
Incoming label 3 has no equal stack top. Push it onto the retained sequence.
The retained stack has 1 label. No adjacent equal pair remains.

review.prompt: For labels [1, 2, 2, 1], which explanation correctly gives a final stack size of zero?

options.text: Canceling the two middle labels exposes the earlier 1 as the top, so the final incoming 1 cancels it.
Cancel only the pair that was adjacent in the original input and leave the two outer labels.
After one pop, stop processing the remaining input because the stack is already reduced.

review.rationale: The stack represents the reduced processed prefix. Pop the matching 2; the resulting top 1 is the only survivor that can cancel the last 1.

transfer.title: Cancel a burst of three
transfer.statement: Change the rule so that three adjacent equal labels cancel. Explain why each stack entry must now remember a run count and why the pair-cancellation implementation cannot be reused unchanged.
transfer.invariant: The stack represents the reduced prefix as runs with counts below three; only the top run can combine with the incoming label.
transfer.expectedReasoning: Store label/count pairs; increment a matching top count and pop when it reaches three. Preserve chain reactions when another run is exposed.
